This likely isn't the answer you're seeking - quite honestly, I use my own personal server (command-line/headless VPS in this case) for anything I want to share. I've actually installed a load of various personal services on it (source code repository, VOIP and such), though I do have a sub-domain set up just for hosting miscellaneous files with Apache. There's no denying that it's an investment (in time, effort, and cash), but the return on that is pure freedom, a trade which I've deemed to be worthwhile.

To use your example of WebM files, Apache doesn't even serve WebM correctly out-of-the-box, not being aware of the correct MIME type for it (video/webm). However, since I am in control of the server, I am free to insert the relevant AddType directive for it (or indeed for any future format).

The truth is that the only reliable service is your own, and of course that freedom (liberty) isn't free (zero-cost). The only thing on which I rely is that my VPS host keeps my box online in return for ~£50 / year, and that I either have or am able to acquire any necessary system admin skills for it.
